chunks: And it is narrated from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said:
I heard Ali عليه السلام saying from the pulpit:

O group of traders, fiqh first, then trade; fiqh first, then trade. By Allah, riba in this ummah is more hidden than the crawling of an ant upon a smooth stone. Protect your wealth through charity. The trader is sinful, and the sinful one is in the Fire, except one who takes what is right and gives what is right.

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةِ: charity; giving in charity as a means of protecting wealth
key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire; punishment in the afterlife
key_terms.الْحَقَّ: what is rightfully due; justice and rightful entitlement in transactions
key_terms.الْفِقْهَ: fiqh; understanding the religious rulings needed before conducting trade
key_terms.لَلرِّبَا: usury; unlawful excess in financial dealings

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam Ali عليه السلام tell traders to learn fiqh before engaging in trade?
ai.summary: This hadith urges traders to learn fiqh before entering commerce, stressing that lawful trade requires religious understanding. It warns that riba can be extremely subtle, encourages protecting wealth through charity, and teaches that salvation in trade lies in taking and giving only what is due in justice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3731 - It is narrated from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah who said:
I heard Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) saying from the pulpit:

"O group of traders! Learn jurisprudence, then engage in trade. Learn jurisprudence, then engage in trade. By Allah (swt), usury in this nation is more hidden than the crawling of an ant on a smooth stone.
Protect your wealth through charity. The trader is sinful, and the sinful one is in the Fire-except the one who takes what is right and gives what is right."
